description: This map illustrates a geometric adjustment process for Natura 2000 (N2K) terrestrial site boundaries, demonstrating an issue related to the Minimum Mapping Unit (MMU) and Minimum Mapping Width (MMW) thresholds. The background is a light yellow area representing the general land. A thin black line indicates an original, problematic boundary that likely contains small, isolated polygons or narrow artefacts falling below the MMU. At a vertex where the black line bends, a small white triangular area represents a 'spike' or an unresolvable geometric feature. A thicker cyan line overlays the black line, depicting the geometrically adjusted and topologically consistent boundary after refinement and buffering operations, resolving the MMU issue. The specific examples for such issues were identified in N2K terrestrial sites located in Finland and Germany. No scale bar, compass, or legend is visible in this highly localised view.
